title: Berlin, One Kiez at a Time

bestPeriod.note: July and August are hot and the city half-empties; January and February are dark by 16:00.

summary: Seven days of Berlin taken district by district, from Museumsinsel to Neukölln, on one weekly BVG ticket and a lot of walking.
hook: Berlin is not a centre with suburbs. It is a loose federation of Kieze, each with its own market hall, its own square and its own century. Treat it that way and the city stops feeling exhausting: one district a day, on foot, with the U-Bahn only to get in and out.

snapshot.Base(s): Kreuzberg (Bergmannkiez) or Mitte, single base all week
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: 65–80 km on foot over seven days, flat, cobbles in the old core
snapshot.Getting There: BER airport, FEX or S9/S45 to the centre in 30–50 min; ICE to Hauptbahnhof
snapshot.Who It Suits: Walkers, museum-goers, anyone who wants a city in cross-section rather than a highlight reel

itinerary.title: Museumsinsel and the Spandauer Vorstadt
itinerary.morning: Start on the island itself. The Neues Museum (August Stüler, 1855; rebuilt by David Chipperfield, 2009) holds Nefertiti, and Chipperfield's decision to leave the war damage legible is the real exhibit. Book a timed slot online; 09:00 and 10:00 release first and go last. The Alte Nationalgalerie (Stüler, 1876) is fifty metres away. Note honestly that the Pergamonmuseum's main building is closed for structural works and is not expected back in full before the late 2020s — the Pergamonmuseum. Das Panorama on Am Kupfergraben covers the gap.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk north into the Spandauer Vorstadt. The Hackesche Höfe (August Endell, 1906) is eight linked courtyards; the first, with its glazed polychrome tile, is the one Endell designed. Continue to Sophienstraße, then the Neue Synagoge on Oranienburger Straße (Eduard Knoblauch and Stüler, 1866), whose gilded dome is visible from three districts.
itinerary.evening: Eat at Zur letzten Instanz on Waisenstraße, a tavern trading since 1621, then walk the Nikolaiviertel after the coach groups have gone.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking · districts: Mitte, Spandauer Vorstadt · tickets approx €26 (Neues Museum + Alte Nationalgalerie).

itinerary.title: Kreuzberg SO36 and the Landwehrkanal
itinerary.morning: Markthalle Neun on Eisenbahnstraße is the anchor: a small weekday market, a full Saturday one, and Street Food Thursday from 17:00 to 22:00. Come early for coffee and Sironi bread, then walk Wrangelkiez.
itinerary.afternoon: Oranienstraße end to end, then Oranienplatz and the Landwehrkanal towpath west to Kottbusser Brücke. If it is a Tuesday or Friday, the Türkischer Markt on Maybachufer runs 11:00–18:00 and is the best value produce in the city.
itinerary.evening: Cross the Oberbaumbrücke (Otto Stahn, 1896) at dusk for the classic Spree view, then back for a beer on Paul-Lincke-Ufer.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km walking · districts: Kreuzberg SO36, Wrangelkiez · tickets approx €0 (markets and streets only).

itinerary.title: Prenzlauer Berg and the Wall at Bernauer Straße
itinerary.morning: The Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer on Bernauer Straße is free, open-air and the only place where the full depth of the border strip — outer wall, death strip, signal fence — is reconstructed. Allow ninety minutes and climb the viewing tower at the documentation centre.
itinerary.afternoon: Kollwitzplatz. The market runs Thursday 12:00–19:00 and Saturday 09:00–16:00. Loop Husemannstraße, Rykestraße and Zionskirchplatz, then the Kulturbrauerei, a Schultheiss brewery complex of 1891 now full of small halls.
itinerary.evening: Konnopke's Imbiss under the U2 viaduct at Eberswalder Straße has been selling Currywurst since 1930. Follow it with a table at the Prater Garten on Kastanienallee, a beer garden since 1837.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walking · districts: Prenzlauer Berg, Gesundbrunnen edge · tickets approx €0 (memorial free).

itinerary.title: Neukölln and Tempelhofer Feld
itinerary.morning: Enter Tempelhofer Feld at the Columbiadamm gate. The runways are public park now; Ernst Sagebiel's terminal (1936–41) is 1.2 km of limestone curve and still one of Europe's largest buildings. Guided tours run several times daily and must be booked ahead.
itinerary.afternoon: Schillerkiez, then Richardplatz — the surviving core of Bohemian Rixdorf, a village settled by Czech Protestants in 1737. Körnerpark, a sunken neo-baroque garden in a former gravel pit, is three streets south.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from Klunkerkranich, the rooftop bar on the Neukölln Arcaden car park, entered by lift from the top parking deck. Small entry fee, queue after 19:00 in summer.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km walking · districts: Neukölln, Rixdorf, Tempelhof · tickets approx €19 (Tempelhof tour).

itinerary.title: Tiergarten, the Kulturforum and Potsdamer Platz
itinerary.morning: Mies van der Rohe's Neue Nationalgalerie (1968, refurbished by Chipperfield in 2021) opens at 10:00; the steel-and-glass upper hall is worth as much time as the collection below. Timed tickets online.
itinerary.afternoon: The Gemäldegalerie next door holds Germany's deepest old-master collection and is almost never full. Then Hans Scharoun's Philharmonie (1963); free lunchtime chamber concerts run Tuesdays in season, doors around 12:00.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Tiergarten paths to the Neuer See, eat at the Café am Neuen See beer garden, and finish at the Siegessäule if the light holds.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking · districts: Tiergarten, Kulturforum, Potsdamer Platz · tickets approx €24 (two state museums, or free with the Museum Pass).

itinerary.title: Friedrichshain and Karl-Marx-Allee
itinerary.morning: Walk Karl-Marx-Allee from Frankfurter Tor to Strausberger Platz. Hermann Henselmann's towers (1952–60) and the tiled Stalinist blocks are the most complete piece of socialist urbanism west of Moscow, and the Café Sibylle at number 72 keeps a small display on the street's history.
itinerary.afternoon: Boxhagener Platz and the RAW-Gelände, a former railway repair yard. The Boxhagener Platz market runs Saturday (food) and Sunday (flea, from 10:00).
itinerary.evening: The East Side Gallery is best walked after 20:00 when the crowds thin. Dinner on Simon-Dach-Straße or at the Volkspark Friedrichshain beer garden.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km walking · districts: Friedrichshain, Stralauer Kiez · tickets approx €0.

itinerary.title: Charlottenburg and City West
itinerary.morning: Schloss Charlottenburg (Johann Arnold Nering, 1699; extended by Eosander and Knobelsdorff) with the Neuer Flügel and the baroque garden. The combined palace ticket is roughly €19.
itinerary.afternoon: Kantstraße for lunch, then the Kaiser-Wilhelm-Gedächtniskirche — Egon Eiermann's 1963 blue-glass hall beside the bombed 1895 tower. Rogacki on Wilmersdorfer Straße, a fish counter since 1928, is the food anchor here.
itinerary.evening: The sixth-floor food hall at KaDeWe, then a last U-Bahn ride east.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walking · districts: Charlottenburg, City West · tickets approx €19.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Oderberger
accommodationStrategy.style: Design hotel in a restored 1902 bathhouse
accommodationStrategy.description: The swimming hall is original and open to guests, which matters after four days of pavement. Oderberger Straße puts Mauerpark, Kastanienallee and the U2 within five minutes, and breakfast runs late enough for a slow start.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 8 weeks ahead, 4 months for a September weekend.

accommodationStrategy.name: Orania.Berlin
accommodationStrategy.description: A 1913 corner building on Oranienplatz with a ground-floor salon and live music most nights. You are inside the Kreuzberg walking radius, which removes a transit leg from three of these days.

accommodationStrategy.name: Michelberger Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: Opposite Warschauer Straße station, so the S-Bahn ring, the U1 and the M10 tram are all at the door. Rooms are small and cheap at the lower tiers; the courtyard kitchen serves late.

logistics.emergency: 112 for fire and ambulance, 110 for police. Pharmacy after hours: the rota is posted in every Apotheke window under Notdienst.
logistics.money: Card acceptance has improved but is not universal: Spätis, Imbiss stands, market halls and some bars are cash-only. Carry €40 in notes.

other.label: Zones
other.text: Berlin runs on AB, BC and ABC. AB covers everything in this itinerary. ABC is only needed for BER airport and Potsdam. If you hold an AB ticket, buy a single Anschlussfahrausweis (extension ticket, approx €2.20) rather than a whole ABC fare.

other.label: The weekly ticket
other.text: The 7-Tage-Karte AB runs approx €43; the ABC version approx €53. A single AB is approx €3.80, a day ticket approx €10.50. The weekly pays for itself on about day four.

other.label: The traps
other.text: There are no barriers. A paper ticket is invalid until stamped in the yellow or red box on the platform or inside the bus or tram — inspectors work in plain clothes and the fine is €60 in cash or on the spot. App tickets (BVG Fahrinfo / Jelbi) validate at purchase, so buy them before you step onto the vehicle, not after. The Kurzstrecke (approx €2.40) is three stops on U- or S-Bahn with no changes, or six stops by bus or tram — it is not a short-distance-in-general ticket.

other.label: Museum Pass Berlin
other.text: is approx €34 for three consecutive days across roughly 30 museums, including everything on Museumsinsel and at the Kulturforum. It does not remove the need for a timed slot: reserve the free entry slot online with the pass number.

other.label: Reichstag dome
other.text: Free but registered. Apply at bundestag.de at least three days ahead — in practice two to three weeks in summer — and bring the passport whose number you registered.

other.label: Sunday closing
other.text: Supermarkets shut; bakeries, Spätis and station shops do not. Museums open Sundays and mostly close Mondays.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 for fire and ambulance, 110 for police. Pharmacy after hours: the rota is posted in every Apotheke window under Notdienst.

proTips: Book the Neues Museum's first slot and go straight to Nefertiti's room; by 11:00 there is a queue at that single gallery door.
The Berliner Philharmoniker release returned and standing seats at the box office 90 minutes before curtain; the acoustic in Scharoun's hall is worth the wait.
Tempelhofer Feld gates close at sunset, times posted at each gate; use Oderstraße in the evening, the last to lock.
Street Food Thursday at Markthalle Neun is heaving by 18:30. Arrive at 17:00 and leave before the door queue forms.
Take the S-Bahn Ring (S41 clockwise) once, all the way round, for 60 minutes and one fare. It is the cheapest architectural survey of the city.
For the Sunday flea markets, Mauerpark is the famous one and Boxhagener Platz is the one where locals actually buy things.

packingNotes: Shoes with a real sole: Berlin's Mitte and Prenzlauer Berg pavements are granite setts and small cobbles.
A rain shell, not an umbrella — the wind across Tempelhofer Feld and the Spree bridges destroys umbrellas.
€40 in small notes and coins for Imbiss stands, Spätis and market halls.
A passport for the Reichstag registration and for ID checks at some club doors.
A refillable bottle; Berliner Wasserbetriebe runs public drinking fountains May to October.
Ear plugs if you take a room facing Oranienstraße, Simon-Dach-Straße or Kastanienallee.
A tote bag for the Türkischer Markt — the stalls do not give out plastic.
whatCouldGoWrong: **You arrive without an ABC ticket at BER.** The airport is in zone C. Buy an ABC single (approx €4.70) at the machine before the platform; the FEX and RE7 to Hauptbahnhof take 30 minutes and run twice hourly.

**A Museumsinsel museum is closed for works.** Beyond the Pergamonmuseum, rotating closures are routine. Check smb.museum the week before and swap in the Gemäldegalerie, the Bode-Museum or the Hamburger Bahnhof.
**A strike or U-Bahn works.** BVG runs replacement buses (SEV) on the same ticket, and the M-series trams cover most U-Bahn corridors. Allow 20 extra minutes at weekends, when closures cluster.
**Rain from noon.** Move the indoor anchor forward: the Kulturforum, the Museum für Naturkunde and the Jüdisches Museum (Daniel Libeskind, 2001) each absorb three hours.
**Refused at a club door.** Normal, not personal. Fall back on a late concert at the Kulturbrauerei or the bars on Weserstraße in Neukölln, which run past 03:00 without a door policy.
